programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo sa bhothan aca gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha i ag iarraidh orra pìosan ealain a chruthachadh le rudan a lorg iad air an tràigh. Saoil dè nì iad? Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them fun challenges. She tasks them with creating works of art from items they found on the beach. What will they make?

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha a’ Chearc Iarainn an-dòchas gum bi cuideigin ann a ghabhas a cuid sgudail. Saoil ciamar a thèid dhi? The Iron Chicken is hopeful that she will find someone who will take her rubbish. How will she get on?

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Double act Phoenix and Mossy are on their way to meet Oona when they find Spiky the hedgehog near the Bat Cave. He is far away from his burrows, and it's getting late. They can't leave him on his own so decide to take him home, but on their way to the Meadow, the friends learn not to judge a book by its very cute cover. Tha 'n dithis charaid, Phoenix is Mosaidh air an slighe a choinneachadh Oona nuair a lorgas iad Spiky a' ghràineag faisg air Uamh nan Ialtag. E astar mòr bho na faichean aige, 's tha 'n oidhch' a' tuiteam.An truaghan beag -e cho beag is leasgardach...do-dhèant' dhaibh fhàgail leis fhèin. Nì iad co-dhùnadh a thoirt dhachaigh, ach air an slighe dhan Achadh, tha an dithis charaid a' tuigs' gum faod mealladh a bhith ceangailt' ri àilleachd.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona and Isabelle are going fishing, so Bernie volunteers to mind Baba and Lala. The little Pufflings are having a great time playing with their ball, and Bernie settles down to watch. When the ball falls into the burrows, Baba and Lala lead Bernie on an underground adventure to find it. There's still life in the old shell yet! Tha Oona is Iseabail a' dol a dh'iasgach, 's tha Bernie ro thoilichte cùram a ghabhail de Bhaba is Lala.Tha na buthaidean beaga nan glòraidh a' cluich leis a' bhall aca, 's tha Bernie ga shocrachadh fhèin 'son an coimhead. Nuair a thèid am ball a-steach dha na faichean, bheir Baba is Lala Bernie air dan'-thuras fo-thalamh 'son am ball a lorg. Tha spionnadh san t-seann t-slige fhathast!

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri iasg agus goiriola! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like a fish and a gorilla!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing ‘s Sula a cluich geama far a bheil an dithis aca a comharrachadh na rudan ‘s fheàrr leotha le bileagan steigeach. Tha iad toilichte rudan diofraicht’ ‘s na h-aon rudan a thaghadh... ‘s e sin gus an cuir Sula billeag air Hoppity Voosh...! Bing and Sula are playing a game where they mark their favourite things by placing a sticky heart-shaped note on it. They are happy to have both different favourites and the same favourites - that is until Sula tags Hoppity Voosh first!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing san amar ‘s tha Flop a’ leughadh sgeulachd dha ach, san ùpraid ullachaidh, tha an leabhar a tuiteam dhan amar ‘s e air a mhilleadh! Tha Bing troimhe chèile ach tha Flop a’ dearbhadh dha g’eil na sgeulachdan ‘s fheàrr nar n-inntinn! Bing is in the bath and wants Flop to read him a story, but in all the commotion, the book falls into the bath and is ruined! Bing is very upset that he won’t get his bedtime story, but Flop proves to him that we keep the best stories in our heads!

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha spòrs aig Daolag-bhreac is Seillean le rudan clòimhteach – cluich an t-Samhraidh. Ladybird and Bee play with fluffy things - summer play.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha Peicein is a charaidean gann de dh’airgead, is leis nach eil ann an airgead ach pìosan beaga pàipeir le dealbhan orra, tha iad uile a’ co-dhùnadh gun cruthaich iad an t-airgead aca fhèin, is gun ceannaich iad na thogras iad. Because they are a little short of money, and considering money notes are only little papers with drawings on them, Petit and his friends decide to create their own money and buy anything they want.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Beileag ag iarraidh dealbh shnog de Phòl agus Anna, ach tha an camara a tha Deòrsa a’ cleachdadh le Granaidh, agus creid e… tha e air a ghonadh le seann mhumaidh crosta. Chan fhada gus an tig e am follais gum bi an camara seo a’ goid anam gach neach a th’ anns gach dealbh a thogas e. Betty wants a nice photo of Dave and Anna, but the camera George uses happens to belong to Gran, and funnily enough…it’s been cursed by an ancient mummy. We soon find out that this camera rather likes stealing the souls of its ‘models’.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Nam biodh dà mhiann aig Pòl, mhiannaicheadh e gum biodh fàileadh nas fheàrr à Mial-mogach agus gum biodh Granaidh na bu laghaiche. Ach ged a gheibheadh Pòl a mhiann, chan eil sin ri ràdh gum biodh cùisean na b’ fheàrr; ’s ann a tha gach miann a’ cur a h-uile sìon bun-os-cionn. Sgudal! If there were two things Dave could wish for it would be for Fuzzypeg to smell fresher, and for Gran to be nicer. But getting what you wish for doesn’t always turn out for the best, and in Dave’s case it sends nature topsy turvy. Rubbish.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: An-diugh, tha Hilda agus Am Fear Fiodh' air cuairt-dànachd mhara - a’ rèiseadh Na Draugen. ‘S ann aig Sealbh a tha fios cò bhuannaicheas! Feumaidh iad a h-uile taic a gheibh iad! Today, Hilda and Am Fear Fiodh are on a high-seas adventure - racing the Draugen. Goodness only knows who will win! They need all the help they can get!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Aig Pàrtaidh Culaidh-Choimhich', tha 'n culaidh-choimheach Bhògais aig Uilidh cho creidsinneach is gu bheil an Rìgh den bheachd gur e a chogais a th' ann an Uilidh. Abair gu bheil Uilidh a' faireachdainn neartmhor leis a' mhealladh! At the Fancy Dress Party, Uilidh’s Bògais costume is so lifelike that the King thinks Uilidh is his conscience. Uilidh feels so powerful as a result of this deception!

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Seachd Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach seachdainn le sgioba-naidheachd BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean à Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Costello MacÌomhair, Maeve NicFhionghain agus Seumas Greumach. Cuideachd, an còisir Soisgeul fo stiùir Gareth Fuller. Bidh Iain fhèin a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail à Tiriodh ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek agus bidh Chloe Steele a’ toirt dhuinn seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Amongst the singers performing are Costello Maciver, Maeve MacKinnon and James Graham. Also appearing is the choir Soisgeul conducted by Gareth Fuller. Iain reflects on his own beliefs with a selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes from Tiree in the company of Donald E Meek, and Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Greim-Bìdh le Gregor
programme.desc: At a community-run growing project, Gregor picks up fresh parsnips. If you can do carrot cake, then why not parsnip cake?

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts the quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams from winning are the ‘Pretenders’, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Anna & Margaret or Marcas & Mia, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Anna & Margaret no Marcas & Mia, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr?

programme.title: Chernobyl – Utopia na Smàl/Chernobyl – Utopia in Flames
programme.desc: Tha iadsan a bha an sàs ann a’ mìneachadh mara thachair air oidhche an 26mh den Ghiblean, 1986, an uair a tha Ionad a Ceithir a spreadhadh. Tha an rud a tha a’ tòiseachadh mar dheuchainn sàbhailteachd àbhaisteach a’ crìochnachadh mar a’ chiad readhachtair niùclasach foillsichte san t-saoghal. Those involved in the events of the night of April 26, 1986, reconstruct them in detail when Chernobyl Unit 4 explodes. What begins as a routine safety test ends in the world's first exposed nuclear reactor. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Tha slighe dùbhlanach aig Somhairle agus a bhràthair Innes air a’ chiad latha aca a’ rothaireachd eadar Inbhir Nis agus Glaschu air an Badger Divide. Somhairle and his brother Innes have a challenging start on their first day cycling between Inverness and Glasgow on the Badger Divide.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Air fhilmeadh aig àm Celtic Connections 2025 agus a’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh a dh’aona ghothach airson Seirm, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Ciorstaidh Pheutan, Eric Bibb, Loudon Wainwright III, Kíla agus Joshua Burnside. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2025, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Ciorstaidh Beaton, Eric Bibb, Loudon Wainwright III, Kíla and Joshua Burnside. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le taisbeanadh air leth bho Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House aig Belladrum 2025 is an còmhlan cliùiteach Albannach, Texas, a’ tilleadh chun na fèise mar phrìomh chòmhlan oidhche Shathairne. Le fuaim leantaileach is guth iongantach Sharleen Spiteri, tha an còmhlan a’ toirt thugainn na h-òrain as fheàrr aca, ’s chan eil leisg air an t-sluagh seinn còmhla riutha. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain MacDonald present from the Hot House Stage at Belladrum as iconic Scottish band Texas return to the festival to headline Saturday night. With their timeless sound and Sharleen Spiteri’s unmistakable vocals, the group perform classic hits, and the crowd need no encouragement to join in.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Marloch, clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads, 2024, ann an Inbhir Nis le An Tèid Thu Leam a Mhàiri am measg nan òran is puirt. Concert set performed by Marloch and originally recorded live at the 2024 Trad Awards in Inverness, with An Tèid Thu Leam a Mhàiri amongst the songs and tunes.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Wildlife on Two
programme.desc: David Attenborough narrates a profile of the pelican, the large water bird noted for its huge pouch and clumsy, waddling gait.

programme.title: The Secret Life of the Sun
programme.desc: Ninety-million miles away from us is the power that shapes our world - the sun. We see it shine in the sky above us, but beyond our sight, something dramatic is happening - the sun is going into overdrive. It's more active now than it's been for a decade, sending eruptions of super-heated plasma and vast waves of radiation towards our planet. With the potential to disrupt our lives in dramatic ways. Using the latest satellite images, and the expertise of Britain's leading solar scientists, Kate Humble and Helen Czerski reveal the inner workings of our very own star, and the influence its mysterious cycles of activity have on our planet. They discover why the light reaching us from the sun can be up to a million years old; they meet the teams who protect us by keeping a round-the-clock vigil on the sun; and investigate why some scientists think longer term changes in the sun's behaviour may have powerful effects on our climate.

programme.title: Inside Classical
programme.desc: The BBC Philharmonic Orchestra and conductor Ben Gernon perform Bruch’s First Violin Concerto and Dvorak’s Symphony No 9, 'From the New World'. Bruch’s romantic violin concerto is performed by Jennifer Pike, who first gained attention in 2002, when at 12 years old, she won the BBC Young Musician competition. She is now in demand as a soloist around the world. Dvorak wrote his Ninth Symphony on a journey of musical discovery around America. It takes inspiration from both native and African-American melodies, and is a cinematic display of orchestral colour that captures the spirit of new discovery.

programme.title: Attenborough's Passion Projects
programme.desc: As part of a season of programming marking Sir David Attenborough's 90th birthday, four of his favourite films are brought together as the renowned naturalist looks back on his personal highlights. First transmitted in 1989, Lost Worlds, Vanished Lives showcases the world's major fossil sites. In a number of specially shot interviews, Attenborough introduces extracts from the series where he reveals ancient sea creatures, sabre-toothed predators and immense dinosaurs. Groundbreaking for its time and still as relevant now, the series explores how fossils fire the imagination and teach us not just about the lives of long-extinct animals, from gentle giants like the brachiosaurs to the greatest predators ever to roam the earth - tyrannosaurs, but also the world they lived in.

programme.title: Darcey Bussell on The Magic of Dance
programme.desc: Renowned ballet dancer Dame Darcey Bussell introduces us to a gem from the BBC’s dance archives, The Magic of Dance, which was first transmitted in 1979 to great acclaim and is presented by celebrated ballet dancer, the unforgettable Margot Fonteyn. Darcey describes her favourite moments of the series, including a tap masterclass with the ever-cool Sammy Davis Jr, a beautiful routine by celebrated Latvian dancer Mikhail Baryshnikov and a glimpse of pioneer of modern dance Isadora Duncan.

programme.title: The Magic of Dance
programme.desc: Margot Fonteyn discusses the role of the male in dance. Her story is illustrated by some of the world's greatest dancers performing some of the era's most enduring dances.

programme.title: Sammy Davis Jr at the BBC
programme.desc: He was known as Mr Entertainment, and it’s clear why that was the case from this collection of some of Sammy Davis Jr’s finest moments on British television - showing off his unbeatable talents as singer and raconteur and opening up about his life in several fascinating conversations. Sammy always had a special affection for the BBC, appearing many times over the years to perform and share stories with the likes of Michael Parkinson and Terry Wogan, and here we find him discussing his encounters with racism and his relationship with America’s civil rights movement, the breakdown of his controversial marriage to the actress May Britt and the car accident that cost him an eye. Alongside all the insights into his life and experiences are, of course, several show-stopping archive performances – as he wows the BBC’s studio audiences with classic songs like Once in a Lifetime, Me and My Shadow and My Funny Valentine.

programme.title: Genius of the Ancient World
programme.desc: In the final episode, Bettany travels to China on the trail of Confucius, a great sage of Chinese history whose ideas have fundamentally shaped the country of his birth for around 2,500 years.

programme.title: TechXplore
programme.desc: The BBC' s sport-loving tech presenter Paul Carter travels to Japan to dive into the Deaflympics, where elite performance meets cutting-edge innovation to smash barriers and supercharge inclusion. Across the deaf competitions, Paul tests universal translation tools that let athletes, staff and fans talk, sign and connect without missing a beat. He hits the athletics track to discover how vibrating starting blocks could shave off vital seconds, and he steps into a fan experience reimagined - from onomatopoeic scoreboards and live social feeds to devices that buzz, glow and thump in time with every moment. Even journeys between Tokyo venues reveal how new tech is helping deaf visitors navigate the city with greater ease. A celebration of tech-driven accessibility and a glimpse of a future where no fan, athlete or sporting moment is left out.

programme.desc: AI Decoded speaks to leading tech podcaster Scott Galloway about the growing controversy surrounding Anthropic's latest AI model, Claude Mythos. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Vick Hope explore the chalk landscapes of the Chilterns, where rare grasslands, seasonal streams and specialised wildlife all depend on the fragile ground beneath their feet. But as habitats have been lost and broken into isolated fragments, some species have declined. Matt meets farmers working together to reconnect these landscapes, helps protect the endangered Duke of Burgundy butterfly and discovers how drone technology is transforming a chalkland vineyard. Vick visits a rare winterbourne stream that flows only after winter rains as restoration work helps bring it back to life. Meanwhile, Adam Henson welcomes a rare-breed middle white pig to his Cotswolds farm and trials crops that could cut fertiliser use.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of Belmont House in sunny Kent, where Fiona opens the show with perfect timing amongst Belmont’s world-famous collection of clocks. Alastair Dickenson is sweet on an immaculate silver honey pot, while Runjeet Singh explores a newly discovered photographic archive revealing the story of Sikh worship in this corner of the county. Raj Bisram is brought a humble piece of wood with links to one of the most notorious British ships in history – HMS Bounty – and recounts a stirring tale of betrayal on the high seas. Cristian Beadman is surprised by a pair of bronze owls, each hiding a saucy secret within, and Fiona foxtrots her way through a chat with dancer and Strictly Come Dancing judge Anton Du Beke.

programme.title: Making Life on Earth: Attenborough's Greatest Adventure
programme.desc: In 1976, David Attenborough embarked on his most ambitious project ever, Life on Earth. No-one had ever attempted a natural history series on this scale before, and David’s reputation was on the line. This is the remarkable story behind the BBC’s most famous wildlife blockbuster. A three-year, hair-raising odyssey around the world, travelling to 40 countries and filming over 600 species, including the famous mountain gorillas. First broadcast in 1979 and watched by 500 million people, it launched David Attenborough’s career as the most successful and influential wildlife film-maker of our time.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Vick Hope explore the chalk landscapes of the Chilterns, where rare grasslands, seasonal streams and specialised wildlife all depend on the fragile ground beneath their feet. Matt meets farmers working together to reconnect these landscapes, helps protect the endangered Duke of Burgundy butterfly and discovers how drone technology is transforming a chalkland vineyard. Meanwhile, Adam Henson welcomes a rare-breed middle white pig to his Cotswolds farm and trials crops that could cut fertiliser use.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of Belmont House in sunny Kent, where Fiona opens the show with perfect timing amongst Belmont’s world-famous collection of clocks. Alastair Dickenson is sweet on an immaculate silver honey pot, while Runjeet Singh explores a newly discovered photographic archive revealing the story of Sikh worship in this corner of the county. Raj Bisram is brought a humble piece of wood with links to one of the most notorious British ships in history – HMS Bounty – and recounts a stirring tale of betrayal on the high seas. Cristian Beadman is surprised by a pair of bronze owls, each hiding a saucy secret within, and Fiona foxtrots her way through a chat with dancer and Strictly Come Dancing judge Anton Du Beke.

programme.title: Making Life on Earth: Attenborough's Greatest Adventure
programme.desc: In 1976, David Attenborough embarked on his most ambitious project ever, Life on Earth. No-one had ever attempted a natural history series on this scale before, and David’s reputation was on the line. This is the remarkable story behind the BBC’s most famous wildlife blockbuster. A three-year, hair-raising odyssey around the world, travelling to 40 countries and filming over 600 species, including the famous mountain gorillas. First broadcast in 1979 and watched by 500 million people, it launched David Attenborough’s career as the most successful and influential wildlife film-maker of our time.

programme.title: The Marvellous Miniature Workshop
programme.desc: Sara Cox and miniaturist Hannah Lemon recreate Manchester’s Crumpsall Library for Leah, a retired social worker who met her late husband there as a teenager. Though the library now lies derelict, Hannah’s intricate model - parquet floors, stained-glass and even Neil’s school cap - brings back its splendour and the love story at its heart.

programme.title: Extraordinary Portraits
programme.desc: A rare medical condition meant Grace was unable to give birth, as she was born without a womb. But in a landmark moment for British medical history, her sister Amy made an extraordinary decision: to donate her womb to her sister in a complicated and involved operation, which lasted hours. Just months after the transplant, Grace became pregnant and now, with her husband, has a healthy daughter. It was a gift that transformed not only the sisters’ lives but those of everyone around them in a story of love, sacrifice and a deep family bond. Bill Bailey pairs Grace and Amy with Karen Turner, an award-winning artist with a powerful commitment to telling women’s stories. Karen works using an unusual and unforgiving technique, painting directly onto raw canvas. With no background layer and no possibility of correction, every paint stroke must be right. As Karen begins her work, she faces a profound challenge: how to capture the depth of love, trust and sacrifice that made this miracle possible. Can she find a way to express not just the medical achievement but the emotional truth behind it and create a portrait worthy of this remarkable act of sisterhood?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Vick Hope explore the chalk landscapes of the Chilterns, where rare grasslands, seasonal streams and specialised wildlife all depend on the fragile ground beneath their feet. But as habitats have been lost and broken into isolated fragments, some species have declined. Matt meets farmers working together to reconnect these landscapes, helps protect the endangered Duke of Burgundy butterfly and discovers how drone technology is transforming a chalkland vineyard. Vick visits a rare winterbourne stream that flows only after winter rains as restoration work helps bring it back to life. Meanwhile, Adam Henson welcomes a rare-breed middle white pig to his Cotswolds farm and trials crops that could cut fertiliser use.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of Belmont House in sunny Kent, where Fiona opens the show with perfect timing amongst Belmont’s world-famous collection of clocks. Alastair Dickenson is sweet on an immaculate silver honey pot, while Runjeet Singh explores a newly discovered photographic archive revealing the story of Sikh worship in this corner of the county. Raj Bisram is brought a humble piece of wood with links to one of the most notorious British ships in history – HMS Bounty – and recounts a stirring tale of betrayal on the high seas. Cristian Beadman is surprised by a pair of bronze owls, each hiding a saucy secret within, and Fiona foxtrots her way through a chat with dancer and Strictly Come Dancing judge Anton Du Beke.

programme.title: Making Life on Earth: Attenborough's Greatest Adventure
programme.desc: In 1976, David Attenborough embarked on his most ambitious project ever, Life on Earth. No-one had ever attempted a natural history series on this scale before, and David’s reputation was on the line. This is the remarkable story behind the BBC’s most famous wildlife blockbuster. A three-year, hair-raising odyssey around the world, travelling to 40 countries and filming over 600 species, including the famous mountain gorillas. First broadcast in 1979 and watched by 500 million people, it launched David Attenborough’s career as the most successful and influential wildlife film-maker of our time.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway visits north Wales and goes into hiding, only to be tracked down by a pair of search and rescue dogs. This walk also has him heading to the hills on a coastal route hundreds of feet up a mountain, trying his hand at golf and learning how a top secret operation near Conwy played a major part in winning the Second World War. His walk takes him from the village of Abergwyngregyn to the quay at Conwy.

programme.title: Extraordinary Portraits
programme.desc: A rare medical condition meant Grace was unable to give birth, as she was born without a womb. But in a landmark moment for British medical history, her sister Amy made an extraordinary decision: to donate her womb to her sister in a complicated and involved operation, which lasted hours. Just months after the transplant, Grace became pregnant and now, with her husband, has a healthy daughter. It was a gift that transformed not only the sisters’ lives but those of everyone around them in a story of love, sacrifice and a deep family bond. Bill Bailey pairs Grace and Amy with Karen Turner, an award-winning artist with a powerful commitment to telling women’s stories. Karen works using an unusual and unforgiving technique, painting directly onto raw canvas. With no background layer and no possibility of correction, every paint stroke must be right. As Karen begins her work, she faces a profound challenge: how to capture the depth of love, trust and sacrifice that made this miracle possible. Can she find a way to express not just the medical achievement but the emotional truth behind it and create a portrait worthy of this remarkable act of sisterhood?

programme.title: The Singer Story: Made in Clydebank
programme.desc: The Singer sewing machine, international icon and a symbol of the Industrial Revolution, helped put the town of Clydebank on the map. Over the course of a century, it employed tens of thousands of 'bankies' before its demise nearly 40 years ago. This documentary charts the story of those workers: how their lives were intertwined with the fortunes of Scotland’s first US multinational company. The programme pays homage to the Singer machine, and the huge impact it made on families and households all over the world.

programme.title: Lockerbie: Our Story
programme.desc: On 21 December 1988, passenger jet Pan Am 103 was blown up over the small Scottish town of Lockerbie, killing 259 on board and 11 on the ground. It was the UK’s largest crime scene and remains the deadliest terrorist attack on British soil. In this documentary, families and loved ones, most of whom are speaking for the first time, tell the deeply personal stories of six victims, each with their own hopes and dreams.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Twilight Monthly magazine needs a new cover star and Victor is convinced he’s the man for the job. Meanwhile, Winston battles with a neighbour to win a stray cat’s affections.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: This episode of the spoof documentary sees Chief Commissioner Miekelson trying out some weapons, getting his portrait painted and doing 'thumbthing' about bigotry. Meanwhile, the rural police deal with a cat stranded in a boat, the urban police aren't fooled by a bluffing burglar and the traffic cops encounter a dozy pedestrian and a sleeping salesman. Volunteer Officer Ken Beattie fines a litterbug on a bridge, Operator Maggie LeBeau tells us about her heroes, and Sergeant Karen Ann Millar is offered fingerprints and some glockenspiel music from local man Bobby Muir.

programme.title: The Sunday Show
programme.desc: Gary Robertson brings you all the main issues from the world of politics and beyond. Big interviews, discussion and analysis of the stories that matter to Scotland.

programme.title: Loop
programme.desc: Moy Mackay draws on the beautiful rural surroundings of the Scottish Borders that she calls home to make her felt artwork. With a nod to the area’s rich textile history, Moy uses traditional crafting techniques combined with a love of painting to create her artworks from merino fleece. A strong believer that art should be for everyone, and that crafts deserve to be acknowledged as art, Moy places textiles in an artworld context in order to highlight their importance. A meditative, thoughtful and intricate process, she often loses herself in the felting. We join Moy in the gently stunning environs of the Tweed Valley, where she draws inspiration for her latest artwork, and then follow her to her local gallery/workshop to watch as she makes one of her unusual felted paintings.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: When the Archer pub reopens after its refurb, Louise, Janet and Donna compete against each other for the job of barmaid. Jonny wins a competition to go shark-jumping in Hawaii, while Gaz desperately tries to do something more exciting than Jonny in Runcorn.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: With Jonny dead, Janet decides she must get through the five stages of grief quickly and Gaz finds a painful way to help her. Donna sets out to prove that she is not what Gaz calls a damp squid. Louise finds a sick way to persuade her friends that she really is pregnant.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda isn't your average girly girl. At 6ft 1in, Miranda gets called 'sir' once too often, much to the amusement of her childhood friend Stevie, who manages Miranda's joke shop. Miranda's mother Penny is disappointed that Miranda runs a joke shop rather than having a proper job. Penny bumps into one of Miranda's old school friends, Tilly, and lies that Miranda has a great new job, so Miranda decides to prove everyone wrong and find a new career. After getting caught by Tilly while helping out as a waitress, she decides to come clean and be proud of her real job, but, thanks to Gary, Tilly jumps to a surprising conclusion about Miranda's employment.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda knows she is not exactly cool, but being young, free and single has its advantages, like jetting off to Thailand on holiday for a few days. Although when it comes down to it, she would rather not bother with the hassle of going quite so far, so she books herself into a hotel across the road instead. She thoroughly enjoys the hotel, and even makes new friends with helpful porter Jason and conference organiser Colin. As her stay goes on, she literally becomes a new woman.

programme.title: Leigh-Anne: Race, Pop and Power
programme.desc: This powerful documentary follows pop star Leigh-Anne Pinnock as she confronts her experience as the only black member of Little Mix, and as a black woman in the music industry. Leigh-Anne talks about the racism she experienced growing up. Both her parents are of Caribbean heritage, and Leigh-Anne identifies as black. She is also aware that having lighter skin and being a celebrity means she is in a more privileged position than others. Leigh-Anne embarks on her own very personal journey to understand how she can use her platform and privilege to combat the profound racism she sees in society around her. After she begins her journey, news of George Floyd’s death and the Black Lives Matter protests start to sweep the world. With the force of a global movement now behind her, Leigh-Anne confronts those closest to her and attempts to bring difficult conversations about black representation right to the top of the music industry.

programme.desc: When the Archer pub reopens after its refurb, Louise, Janet and Donna compete against each other for the job of barmaid. Jonny wins a competition to go shark-jumping in Hawaii, while Gaz desperately tries to do something more exciting than Jonny in Runcorn.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: With Jonny dead, Janet decides she must get through the five stages of grief quickly and Gaz finds a painful way to help her. Donna sets out to prove that she is not what Gaz calls a damp squid. Louise finds a sick way to persuade her friends that she really is pregnant.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda isn't your average girly girl. At 6ft 1in, Miranda gets called 'sir' once too often, much to the amusement of her childhood friend Stevie, who manages Miranda's joke shop. Miranda's mother Penny is disappointed that Miranda runs a joke shop rather than having a proper job. Penny bumps into one of Miranda's old school friends, Tilly, and lies that Miranda has a great new job, so Miranda decides to prove everyone wrong and find a new career. After getting caught by Tilly while helping out as a waitress, she decides to come clean and be proud of her real job, but, thanks to Gary, Tilly jumps to a surprising conclusion about Miranda's employment.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda knows she is not exactly cool, but being young, free and single has its advantages, like jetting off to Thailand on holiday for a few days. Although when it comes down to it, she would rather not bother with the hassle of going quite so far, so she books herself into a hotel across the road instead. She thoroughly enjoys the hotel, and even makes new friends with helpful porter Jason and conference organiser Colin. As her stay goes on, she literally becomes a new woman.

programme.desc: Max attempts to court Cindy, Walford welcomes a surprise visitor, and the Gulatis and the Panesars try to support Ravi.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: The Mitchells try to get through to Phil, Cindy and Max have a close call, and the Slaters surprise Big Mo.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Phil’s search continues, two Walford residents face a race against time, and Nigel receives some visitors.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Albert Square comes together to celebrate a friend, Phil battles his inner demons, and Max and Cindy’s romance causes friction.

programme.title: Leigh-Anne: Race, Pop and Power
programme.desc: This powerful documentary follows pop star Leigh-Anne Pinnock as she confronts her experience as the only black member of Little Mix, and as a black woman in the music industry. Leigh-Anne talks about the racism she experienced growing up. Both her parents are of Caribbean heritage, and Leigh-Anne identifies as black. She is also aware that having lighter skin and being a celebrity means she is in a more privileged position than others. Leigh-Anne embarks on her own very personal journey to understand how she can use her platform and privilege to combat the profound racism she sees in society around her. After she begins her journey, news of George Floyd’s death and the Black Lives Matter protests start to sweep the world. With the force of a global movement now behind her, Leigh-Anne confronts those closest to her and attempts to bring difficult conversations about black representation right to the top of the music industry.

programme.title: The Woman in Black
programme.desc: A young solicitor travels to a remote village, where he discovers that the vengeful ghost of a scorned woman is terrorizing the locals.

programme.title: Paranormal
programme.desc: Sian dives into the case of medium Helen Duncan and the claims she could summon the dead. She starts in Helen’s birthplace, Callander, a small town where her childhood premonitions caused fear.

programme.title: Paranormal
programme.desc: Disturbed by a recording of what appears to be a spirit voice and accounts of Helen summoning physical spirit forms, Sian focuses on evidence from those who believed it to be fake.

programme.title: Paranormal
programme.desc: Sian finds one of a handful of mediums who claim they bring back spirits in physical form. This could be a glimpse into Helen’s world, but Sian’s been warned there are dangers.

programme.title: Mint
programme.desc: It’s ladies day at the races. Cat has to make a speech, and it forces her to confront what she has been denying about her relationship with Dylan. Ollie misbehaves. With alcohol and adrenaline in the air, it’s not long before rivalries are stirred up and best behaviour gives way to chaos. Shannon and Arran are caught in the crossfire as their families violently collide.

programme.title: Mint
programme.desc: As Dylan rages at Shannon in the wake of ladies day, she escapes and spends a life-changing day with Arran. Spending time together in a world of their own, they grow closer than ever. Meanwhile, tensions erupt between Cat and Dylan, making them question the foundations of their life together. Can they find a way to salvage what they have built? And will the family survive what comes next?

programme.title: The Cage
programme.desc: When Matty and Leanne catch each other stealing from their casino, they agree to stop. But as their lives spiral out of control, the pact they have made frays.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Take a Hike
programme.desc: This week, we’re in the Highlands and Islands of splendid Scotland. It’s home to five keen walkers, all hoping to walk off with the prize. Today, it’s 40-year-old Cathy’s turn to lead the walk. She moved to the Isle of Mull three years ago, where she works as a technical manager in a biscuit factory. She’s planned a coastal walk from the picture-postcard town of Tobermory (recognisable as the setting for the children’s series Balamory). As an adopted Scot, she’s opted for some traditional Scottish activities to entertain the group. Can Cathy wow the walkers with the charms of Mull and win all the points?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson and Sammi Kinghorn head to the Vale of Evesham, where fertile soils and a mild microclimate have long made it one of Britain’s most productive growing regions. Early spring brings the so-called hungry gap, but the vale has a long history of producing food, even in these leaner months. From the first spears of its world-famous asparagus to high-tech growers producing food year round, and from historic market gardens to traditional orchards alive with early pollinators, Adam and Sammi explore a landscape shaped by both tradition and innovation. While fresh produce may be scarce elsewhere, the Vale of Evesham is already beginning to flourish. Meanwhile, Charlotte Smith investigates how falling milk prices are leading some dairy farmers to call it a day, despite record exports and booming milk production.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie visits a dairy farm near Torthorwald in Dumfriesshire at calving time. With 700 newborns due, he finds out about the benefits of block calving. Meanwhile, Shahbaz visits the seal colony in the Ythan Estuary in Aberdeenshire to find out how drones are being used for conservation, and Arlene is in Easter Ross to meet a woman who has been raising menopause awareness. Cammy is on home turf in Ayrshire as early potato planting gets under way, and as Landward continues to celebrate 50 years on air, Anne revisits a story from the archive that features cattle with a very unusual colour.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: There is lots of planting for the plate at Beechgrove Garden as Kirsty Wilson and Brian Cunningham start growing a wide variety of edible produce. Kirsty is the first of the Beechgrove team to kick off work on her competition plot. Each presenter has been given a sense to appeal to in each of their competition borders, and Kirsty is planting things that will taste fantastic. She is also trying something new to Beechgrove: hops. Meanwhile, Brian provides an update on the veg he sowed at the start of the series and is in his rain garden checking on what survived this year's wet weather. There are all the usual handy hints, and there is a visit to Calum Clunie’s allotment in Leven.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Poppy O’Toole makes her prepares a brilliant weeknight supper of tikka salmon, spiced new potatoes and a cooling cucumber salad. Joe Hurd brings a taste of Sicily to the studio with stracchino-stuffed lamb chops with a side of the classic Italian caponata, all inspired by the late, great Antonio Carluccio. Ols Halas swaps the circus for the kitchen as he rustles up pork belly buns with poached rhubarb and dirty fries, while Jack Croft and Will Murray reveal the secrets to their most popular restaurant dish – confit cabbage with chestnuts, crispy cabbage leaves and vibrant wild garlic sauce. Chris Stark does work experience at the French Ambassador’s Residence for a crash course in fine dining. Greg Davies tucks into either his food heaven, beef, or his food hell, seafood! Meanwhile, Rick Stein gets his hands dirty digging for Cornish spuds, and Clive Myrie enjoys an aphrodisiac in the Dominican Republic.

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: Andi is in Bristol to help Jasper Thompson, a local man whose pioneering homeless project transforms shipping containers into temporary accommodation. He wants to raise awareness about his new community cafe, so who better than Andi to help him put on an unforgettable launch party with a Caribbean flavour? To entice locals to the event and kick off the cafe with a bang, Andi must put together a unique and delicious feast that draws on her and Jasper’s own roots in Antigua and Jamaica while also paying tribute to Bristol’s wider Caribbean heritage, using only the best local produce. The cafe itself needs a complete refurb, but can Jasper get it ready in time, and can Andi harness the Bristolians' unique creative spirit to make sure the event’s a roaring success?

programme.title: Grand Hotel
programme.desc: During an eventful few days, the luxurious Grand Hotel in Berlin hosts the intersecting lives of a diverse group of guests, including a Russian ballerina fearful that her career is waning, a penniless baron, a terminally ill accountant and a powerful Prussian businessman desperate to make a deal. Classic star-studded drama from MGM studios.

During the First World War, two soldiers are ordered across no-man's-land and deep into enemy territory to deliver a message. If they fail, an entire battalion, under the mistaken belief the Germans are retreating, will be ordered over the top and into a deadly trap.

programme.title: Here We Are
programme.desc: Aharon has devoted his life to raising his son Uri, where they live together in a gentle routine away from the real world. But Uri is autistic and now as a young adult it might be time for him to live in a specialised home. But Aharon feels deep down that Uri is not ready for this separation, so on the way to the home, decides to run away with his son and they hit the road. A journey that has unexpected consequences for Aharon and Uri’s quiet life together. In Hebrew with English subtitles.

programme.title: The Championship
programme.desc: The Ulster Senior Football Championship reaches the semi-final stage as the counties go head-to-head for a place in the final and a chance of winning the coveted Anglo Celt. Sarah Mulkerrins presents full match coverage, with expert analysis from a panel of experts. Commentary is by Thomas Niblock and Conor McManus, with pitch-side updates from Orla Bannon.

programme.title: The Chronicles of Armagh
programme.desc: Narrated by Colin Morgan, The Chronicles of Armagh follows a year in the less urban parts of an ancient city and its surrounding villages, where people’s lives are rooted in nature and the seasons that shape it.

programme.title: Paula McIntyre’s Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: Paula cooks up a healthy version of a sausage roll with carrot ketchup on the side. She meets a highland dance teacher and her father in Bready near Strabane, both novice cooks, and shows them how to make the perfect barbecue lamb kebabs with a minty broad bean dip. There is a touch of nostalgia about the final pudding of the series: Paula makes individual brown lemonade cakes filled with a gooseberry and elderflower cream.

programme.desc: Mark Carruthers looks at the political developments of the week and questions policymakers on the key issues.

Today, it’s 40-year-old Cathy’s turn to lead the walk. She moved to the Isle of Mull three years ago, where she works as a technical manager in a biscuit factory. She’s planned a coastal walk from the picture-postcard town of Tobermory (recognisable as the setting for the children’s series Balamory). programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson and Sammi Kinghorn head to the Vale of Evesham, where fertile soils and a mild microclimate have long made it one of Britain’s most productive growing regions. Early spring brings the so-called hungry gap, but the vale has a long history of producing food, even in these leaner months. From the first spears of its world-famous asparagus to high-tech growers producing food year round, and from historic market gardens to traditional orchards alive with early pollinators, Adam and Sammi explore a landscape shaped by both tradition and innovation. While fresh produce may be scarce elsewhere, the Vale of Evesham is already beginning to flourish. Meanwhile, Charlotte Smith investigates how falling milk prices are leading some dairy farmers to call it a day, despite record exports and booming milk production.

programme.desc: Happy notices a tiny fruit fly on his apple, and the Squirrels are amazed by how small it is. programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It's lovely and warm - just right for a day on the beach. The Squirrels learn how to make sandcastles - dig, dig, dig! They are doing such a good job that Jon and Nigel ask the crabs if the Squirrels could work together to build them a new home. They create the most spectacular giant sandcastle ever seen, with shells, seaweed, great views and lots of sand.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventures with Captain Barnacles and his explorers. Only Peso can save the day when a cone snail invades the Octopod.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Tidbit is very serious about using sunscreen and even asks Vida to apply it to his shell. But when he gets distracted while having fun in the sun, a sunburn appears and he needs Vida’s help again.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Animated adventure comedy series. How will the Go Jetters retrieve Xuli's treasured 'Academy Ace' flying trophy from Caernarfon Castle?

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi and Aunty T visit the Manchester Museum. Rafi thinks dinosaurs are more than fine and wishes for a real one. Suddenly, Slurpy the triceratops appears! Slurpy is cheeky - he slurps faces, leaves colourful footprints and knocks things over while munching salad. Rafi worries about the mess, but Aunty T laughs and enjoys the fun. When the wish ends, Slurpy disappears, and Aunty T uses her own wand to put the museum back together. She admits dinosaurs and museums are magic, and Rafi beams with delight.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: A famous soul singer is coming to perform in the garden, but no one knows what they look like. Meanwhile, a cheeky little mouse with a great big voice has appeared in the Sunhouse.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s Chicory running the show backstage and singing about how she, the Belgian Endive, was discovered in the song Chicory, Dickory, Dock!

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends enjoy a day exploring the forest, whilst Mr Tumble goes on a nature hunt with Tumble Ted.

programme.title: The Toddler Club
programme.desc: Nigel, Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear welcome toddlers Joshua, Inam, Liyana, Maisy, Francis and Arabella, and their grown-ups, to the Toddler Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! The What’s in the Box? game reveals a pair of stripy socks, and when the toddlers and parents open up a bigger box, they discover lots more objects and toys that are inspired by patterns. This theme is explored through play, song and story. Grown-ups are encouraged to take part at home by hiding a safe, toddler-appropriate patterns toy or object inside a recycled box for them to reveal and explore with their toddler. Storytime is all about discovering new words, as Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear draw different patterns at home and outside. From zigzags in the mud to swirls in the bath bubbles, the twins have lots of arty fun! Viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring the patterns theme too. Plus, The Circle Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with stretching and the Goodbye song.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Moa’s chick is reluctant to emerge from her egg, so Kiri sings an encouraging song.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: The Piggies can’t decide between playing outside or staying inside with a board game, so Charlie comes up with the perfect idea - a giant board game to play outside! The game is wild and fun, but the three Piggies get so competitive that they don’t have much fun at all.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: It’s Elba’s birthday and sister Iona is planning a very special tea party for her. Iona and Elba decorate the bedroom ready for the big party, and there are lots of balloons and games to enjoy. But Iona and Mum have a secret planned, and Elba is surprised when a robot arrives at the door with her favourite chocolate cake!

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Stanley poses for a portrait in the town art class, but he has other jobs to do. Can he stay still long enough for everyone to finish their artwork?

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers land on a forested planet and learn to play a game called impish ball. But before they can start, they must help the locals build a nest while distracting a mischievous beaverling.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Pea-Rexes must rescue Rud, who's stuck in the snow.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Mrs Hobbs challenges the After Schoolers to vote for their favourite activity - and to do it again on Mr Brooklyn-Bell's arrival.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Novah, Nelly and Aaron are all ears as they discover lots of different sounds in the city centre garden - from tweeting birds and rustling leaves, to cars and a crane!

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: Tom likes to do big things but struggles when Professor Kranium shrinks him with her ray.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers learn why rock piles are an important place for lots of creatures to rest, keep cool or bathe in the sun. They gather lots of rocks and get to work, building their very own ‘rock city’ – a wonderful habitat for insects and minibeasts .

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Andy and Jen are on an epic adventure to discover what the dinosaurs of Dino Island get up to at night. When Andy loses his gizmo and gets lost in the dark, a friendly velociraptor comes to his aid. Along the way, Andy spots a T rex and narrowly avoids being stomped on by a herd of Alamosaurus, who are protecting their eggs.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato and Chilli are playing a computer game called Dino Defenders 2: Galactic Space Showdown. But just as they are about to win, Evil Pea snatches it away. They try to get it back, but she jumps into a toy version of the Big Bad Spaceship from the game and shoots energy balls at them, turning the supermarket shelves into a real version of the game! Despite their best efforts, they just can’t get past the energy balls. However, Supertato has an idea to use a toy version of a Dino Defender to climb the shelves and beat Evil Pea in the Big Bad Spaceship!

programme.title: Magic Hands

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Fergie’s wheelchair breaks from doing an awesome trick, Vida asks Grandpa Beaver to make her a new one so that she can get even better and do more tricks.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: When Cosima wrongly accuses Big Lizard of eating Dad's birthday cake, he vanishes. Has he run away, or is he planning a special surprise to save the day?

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Ruby and Finn struggle to score in basketball, so Rafi wishes for a magic ball. At first, it’s fun, as every shot goes in - even trick throws. But the constant winning becomes boring, and the ball bounces endlessly into the hoop by itself. The trio try to contain it, but it escapes again and again. Finally, they return to playing with the ordinary ball, and Finn sinks a real shot, proving true victory is earned.

programme.title: Bluey

programme.desc: A photo of Gran Gran and JoJo’s mummy when she was a little girl inspires them to take a walk and compare old photos of their neighbourhood to see how it has changed over time.

programme.desc: Ava’s solar gadgets malfunction, making her doubt her skills. But with PC Plum’s encouragement, she realises that each invention needs a different-sized solar panel.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It's lovely and warm - just right for a day on the beach. The Squirrels learn how to make sandcastles - dig, dig, dig! They are doing such a good job that Jon and Nigel ask the crabs if the Squirrels could work together to build them a new home. They create the most spectacular giant sandcastle ever seen, with shells, seaweed, great views and lots of sand.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventures with Captain Barnacles and his explorers. Only Peso can save the day when a cone snail invades the Octopod.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Tidbit is very serious about using sunscreen and even asks Vida to apply it to his shell. But when he gets distracted while having fun in the sun, a sunburn appears and he needs Vida’s help again.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Animated adventure comedy series. How will the Go Jetters retrieve Xuli's treasured 'Academy Ace' flying trophy from Caernarfon Castle?

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi and Aunty T visit the Manchester Museum. Rafi thinks dinosaurs are more than fine and wishes for a real one. Suddenly, Slurpy the triceratops appears! Slurpy is cheeky - he slurps faces, leaves colourful footprints and knocks things over while munching salad. Rafi worries about the mess, but Aunty T laughs and enjoys the fun. When the wish ends, Slurpy disappears, and Aunty T uses her own wand to put the museum back together. She admits dinosaurs and museums are magic, and Rafi beams with delight.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: A famous soul singer is coming to perform in the garden, but no one knows what they look like. Meanwhile, a cheeky little mouse with a great big voice has appeared in the Sunhouse.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s Chicory running the show backstage and singing about how she, the Belgian Endive, was discovered in the song Chicory, Dickory, Dock!

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends enjoy a day exploring the forest, whilst Mr Tumble goes on a nature hunt with Tumble Ted.

programme.title: The Toddler Club
programme.desc: Nigel, Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear welcome toddlers Joshua, Inam, Liyana, Maisy, Francis and Arabella, and their grown-ups, to the Toddler Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! The What’s in the Box? game reveals a pair of stripy socks, and when the toddlers and parents open up a bigger box, they discover lots more objects and toys that are inspired by patterns. This theme is explored through play, song and story. Grown-ups are encouraged to take part at home by hiding a safe, toddler-appropriate patterns toy or object inside a recycled box for them to reveal and explore with their toddler. Storytime is all about discovering new words, as Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear draw different patterns at home and outside. From zigzags in the mud to swirls in the bath bubbles, the twins have lots of arty fun! Viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring the patterns theme too. Plus, The Circle Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with stretching and the Goodbye song.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Moa’s chick is reluctant to emerge from her egg, so Kiri sings an encouraging song.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: The Piggies can’t decide between playing outside or staying inside with a board game, so Charlie comes up with the perfect idea - a giant board game to play outside! The game is wild and fun, but the three Piggies get so competitive that they don’t have much fun at all.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: It’s Elba’s birthday and sister Iona is planning a very special tea party for her. Iona and Elba decorate the bedroom ready for the big party, and there are lots of balloons and games to enjoy. But Iona and Mum have a secret planned, and Elba is surprised when a robot arrives at the door with her favourite chocolate cake!

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Stanley poses for a portrait in the town art class, but he has other jobs to do. Can he stay still long enough for everyone to finish their artwork?

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers land on a forested planet and learn to play a game called impish ball. But before they can start, they must help the locals build a nest while distracting a mischievous beaverling.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Pea-Rexes must rescue Rud, who's stuck in the snow.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Mrs Hobbs challenges the After Schoolers to vote for their favourite activity - and to do it again on Mr Brooklyn-Bell's arrival.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Novah, Nelly and Aaron are all ears as they discover lots of different sounds in the city centre garden - from tweeting birds and rustling leaves, to cars and a crane!

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: Tom likes to do big things but struggles when Professor Kranium shrinks him with her ray.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers learn why rock piles are an important place for lots of creatures to rest, keep cool or bathe in the sun. They gather lots of rocks and get to work, building their very own ‘rock city’ – a wonderful habitat for insects and minibeasts .

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Andy and Jen are on an epic adventure to discover what the dinosaurs of Dino Island get up to at night. When Andy loses his gizmo and gets lost in the dark, a friendly velociraptor comes to his aid. Along the way, Andy spots a T rex and narrowly avoids being stomped on by a herd of Alamosaurus, who are protecting their eggs.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato and Chilli are playing a computer game called Dino Defenders 2: Galactic Space Showdown. But just as they are about to win, Evil Pea snatches it away. They try to get it back, but she jumps into a toy version of the Big Bad Spaceship from the game and shoots energy balls at them, turning the supermarket shelves into a real version of the game! Despite their best efforts, they just can’t get past the energy balls. However, Supertato has an idea to use a toy version of a Dino Defender to climb the shelves and beat Evil Pea in the Big Bad Spaceship!

programme.title: Magic Hands
programme.desc: Bobbles and friends play games, run amok and feast on a delicious picnic in the forest whilst Aimee and Mia perform ‘The Teddy Bears' Picnic’. In British Sign Language, accompanied by animations.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: It's curry night, and Nick writes a song to help him remember to buy lots of healthy ingredients, but will he remember to buy Norman's dog treats?

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Fergie’s wheelchair breaks from doing an awesome trick, Vida asks Grandpa Beaver to make her a new one so that she can get even better and do more tricks.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: When Cosima wrongly accuses Big Lizard of eating Dad's birthday cake, he vanishes. Has he run away, or is he planning a special surprise to save the day?

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Ruby and Finn struggle to score in basketball, so Rafi wishes for a magic ball. At first, it’s fun, as every shot goes in - even trick throws. But the constant winning becomes boring, and the ball bounces endlessly into the hoop by itself. The trio try to contain it, but it escapes again and again. Finally, they return to playing with the ordinary ball, and Finn sinks a real shot, proving true victory is earned.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: At a party, Bingo is desperate to show off her handstand skills.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: A photo of Gran Gran and JoJo’s mummy when she was a little girl inspires them to take a walk and compare old photos of their neighbourhood to see how it has changed over time.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah and Duck give Moon painting lessons after being inspired by a trip to the art gallery.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Children's animation. Charlie loves his little sister Lola, even if she gets carried away by her imagination sometimes! Lola and Lotta are best, best friends. They do everything together - until a new girl arrives at school. Lola feels left out until Charlie and Marv help her realise that Lotta is still her best friend.

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: Inside the little toy house, the friends discover the rhyme Old King Cole in the nursery rhyme book. When Mr Onion wishes he could be a merry king like Old King Cole, they all have to work together to make Old King Onion the merriest king of all.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa think they’ve found a butterfly but are surprised to learn that it’s a moth - it sleeps during the day and comes out to play at night. At Play Time, they shine a toy torch into dark places and accidentally disturb the moth. It follows them to Yummy Land, where the Yummies help the friends learn more about nocturnal life, gifting them a moon flower that only opens at night.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: After waking Upsy Daisy, Igglepiggle goes with her for a walk in the garden. Upsy Daisy's bed decides to follow them even when they ride on the Ninky Nonk. When Upsy Daisy decides she would like a rest, her bed makes her chase after it.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Fum, the littlest member of the Crumb family, is missing! Join Arthur Darvill as he takes us on an adventure with the rest of the Crumb family to find him.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton presents the series where she meets the owners of beloved pets who have appointments at The Grove Vets. The appointment book is full in this episode as through the doors this time comes 18-year-old cat Paws, whose loss of weight is concerning his owner, Zina the Pomeranian - who is booked in for a spay - and Mara the Boston Terrier, who is undergoing some vital high-tech eye treatment. Elsewhere, whoever has heard of a Labrador being off their food? Dr James Greenwood swaps being a vet to become a detective as he tries to uncover why Rusty is presenting as the saddest dog in the world - who has also, worryingly, lost his appetite - and we meet two owners who go to great lengths to help their dogs' mobility by booking them into a specialist hydrotherapy clinic.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. James then finds himself welcomed into a bouchon, a rustic Lyon institution where he's served a slice of local history in the form of a machon - after experiencing the heartier fare of the region, James ventures to one of the city's many Michelin-starred restaurants to experience some fine dining. James then uses Lyon's inspiration to cook up a tasty pork dish with Lyonnaise potatoes - back in his own kitchen, he then draws on the rustic style of cookery he saw at the bouchon for a rich game terrine and shows us how to make one of France's best-known desserts of creme brulee.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh heads to Swindon in this episode to surprise Lorraine, a retired RAF servicewoman and devoted charity volunteer. Lorraine struggles with mobility issues because of a spinal injury and lives with her full-time support team Poppy and Doris, who are both Leonberger dogs - Poppy is a retired therapy dog and Doris is Lorraine's assistance dog who helps with chores such as laundry and fetching household items. The team creates a fabulous low-maintenance garden as a calming retreat for both Lorraine and her canine family, Alan shares the secrets of creating a cut-price chamomile lawn, and Katie creates a Love Your Garden first: a dramatic water feature that doubles as a doggie-paddling pool.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. programme.title: The Tower
programme.desc: Crime thriller. Nearly two years since we last saw Sarah Collins, we catch up with her as she is called to the brutal stabbing of a teenager - her investigation soon finds itself at cross purposes with a covert operation led by Kieran Shaw, who is working with Sarah's old partner Steve Bradshaw while he is now deep undercover. Meanwhile, Lizzie Adama is back at Farlow trying to balance her new role as a detective with family life, but her path and Kieran's are about to cross.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton presents the series where she meets the owners of beloved pets who have appointments at The Grove Vets. The appointment book is full in this episode as through the doors this time comes 18-year-old cat Paws, whose loss of weight is concerning his owner, Zina the Pomeranian - who is booked in for a spay - and Mara the Boston Terrier, who is undergoing some vital high-tech eye treatment. Elsewhere, whoever has heard of a Labrador being off their food? Dr James Greenwood swaps being a vet to become a detective as he tries to uncover why Rusty is presenting as the saddest dog in the world - who has also, worryingly, lost his appetite - and we meet two owners who go to great lengths to help their dogs' mobility by booking them into a specialist hydrotherapy clinic.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. James then finds himself welcomed into a bouchon, a rustic Lyon institution where he's served a slice of local history in the form of a machon - after experiencing the heartier fare of the region, James ventures to one of the city's many Michelin-starred restaurants to experience some fine dining. James then uses Lyon's inspiration to cook up a tasty pork dish with Lyonnaise potatoes - back in his own kitchen, he then draws on the rustic style of cookery he saw at the bouchon for a rich game terrine and shows us how to make one of France's best-known desserts of creme brulee.

programme.title: James Martin's Saturday Morning
programme.desc: James is joined at his house in the Hampshire countryside by presenter, DJ and I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! star Kelly Brook, chefs Tommy Banks and Alex Dilling, and forager Alysia Vasey.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Joining Alan Titchmarsh at Manor Farm this Bank Holiday weekend are Stephen and Anita Mangan, Rita Tushingham and royal biographer Robert Hardman. Horticulturalist Camilla Bassett-Smith opens the pages of her May Diary, urban birder David Lindo gets up close and personal with some coots, and drinks expert Tom Surgey has some afternoon tea-inspired tipples. Plus, shire horses Percy and Frank reveal a very special talent.

programme.title: Josie's Taste Of The Westcountry
programme.desc: Proud Bristolian Josie Gibson takes us on a tour of her beloved West Country in a journey of celebration to discover dinner delights, freshly-caught lunches, the best of passionate artisan makers and growers and a few hidden gems to surprise us all - in this episode, Josie heads to Somerset. A county of apples and cheese where ancient caves and landscapes continue to inspire visitors, Josie boards a traditional train to explore the magnificent Somerset coast, gets lessons in oyster-shucking and cider-making, and discovers the secrets of Cheddar Gorge.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh heads to Swindon in this episode to surprise Lorraine, a retired RAF servicewoman and devoted charity volunteer. Lorraine struggles with mobility issues because of a spinal injury and lives with her full-time support team Poppy and Doris, who are both Leonberger dogs - Poppy is a retired therapy dog and Doris is Lorraine's assistance dog who helps with chores such as laundry and fetching household items. The team creates a fabulous low-maintenance garden as a calming retreat for both Lorraine and her canine family, Alan shares the secrets of creating a cut-price chamomile lawn, and Katie creates a Love Your Garden first: a dramatic water feature that doubles as a doggie-paddling pool.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton presents the series where she meets the owners of beloved pets who have appointments at The Grove Vets. The appointment book is full in this episode as through the doors this time comes 18-year-old cat Paws, whose loss of weight is concerning his owner, Zina the Pomeranian - who is booked in for a spay - and Mara the Boston Terrier, who is undergoing some vital high-tech eye treatment. Elsewhere, whoever has heard of a Labrador being off their food? Dr James Greenwood swaps being a vet to become a detective as he tries to uncover why Rusty is presenting as the saddest dog in the world - who has also, worryingly, lost his appetite - and we meet two owners who go to great lengths to help their dogs' mobility by booking them into a specialist hydrotherapy clinic.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. James then finds himself welcomed into a bouchon, a rustic Lyon institution where he's served a slice of local history in the form of a machon - after experiencing the heartier fare of the region, James ventures to one of the city's many Michelin-starred restaurants to experience some fine dining. James then uses Lyon's inspiration to cook up a tasty pork dish with Lyonnaise potatoes - back in his own kitchen, he then draws on the rustic style of cookery he saw at the bouchon for a rich game terrine and shows us how to make one of France's best-known desserts of creme brulee.

A county of apples and cheese where ancient caves and landscapes continue to inspire visitors, Josie boards a traditional train to explore the magnificent Somerset coast, gets lessons in oyster-shucking and cider-making, and discovers the secrets of Cheddar Gorge.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh heads to Swindon in this episode to surprise Lorraine, a retired RAF servicewoman and devoted charity volunteer. Lorraine struggles with mobility issues because of a spinal injury and lives with her full-time support team Poppy and Doris, who are both Leonberger dogs - Poppy is a retired therapy dog and Doris is Lorraine's assistance dog who helps with chores such as laundry and fetching household items. The team creates a fabulous low-maintenance garden as a calming retreat for both Lorraine and her canine family, Alan shares the secrets of creating a cut-price chamomile lawn, and Katie creates a Love Your Garden first: a dramatic water feature that doubles as a doggie-paddling pool.

programme.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
programme.desc: Heart-warming sci-fi adventure. After a gentle alien becomes stranded on Earth, the being is discovered and befriended by a young boy called Elliott. Bringing the extra-terrestrial into his suburban California house, Elliott calls the alien E.T. and introduces it to his brother Michael and his little sister Gertie - the children decide to keep its existence a secret. When E.T. falls ill, however, the US government intervenes - and a dire situation follows for both Elliott and the alien.

programme.title: The Dark Knight
programme.desc: Oscar-winning action crime drama sequel. Bruce Wayne - also known as the Caped Crusader - must now face one of the greatest psychological tests of his ability to fight injustice in order to come out on top once more...

programme.title: The Tower
programme.desc: Crime thriller. Nearly two years since we last saw Sarah Collins, we catch up with her as she is called to the brutal stabbing of a teenager - her investigation soon finds itself at cross purposes with a covert operation led by Kieran Shaw, who is working with Sarah's old partner Steve Bradshaw while he is now deep undercover. Meanwhile, Lizzie Adama is back at Farlow trying to balance her new role as a detective with family life, but her path and Kieran's are about to cross.

programme.title: Unwind with ITV

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton presents the series where she meets the owners of beloved pets who have appointments at The Grove Vets. The appointment book is full in this episode as through the doors this time comes 18-year-old cat Paws, whose loss of weight is concerning his owner, Zina the Pomeranian - who is booked in for a spay - and Mara the Boston Terrier, who is undergoing some vital high-tech eye treatment. Elsewhere, whoever has heard of a Labrador being off their food? Dr James Greenwood swaps being a vet to become a detective as he tries to uncover why Rusty is presenting as the saddest dog in the world - who has also, worryingly, lost his appetite - and we meet two owners who go to great lengths to help their dogs' mobility by booking them into a specialist hydrotherapy clinic.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. James then finds himself welcomed into a bouchon, a rustic Lyon institution where he's served a slice of local history in the form of a machon - after experiencing the heartier fare of the region, James ventures to one of the city's many Michelin-starred restaurants to experience some fine dining. James then uses Lyon's inspiration to cook up a tasty pork dish with Lyonnaise potatoes - back in his own kitchen, he then draws on the rustic style of cookery he saw at the bouchon for a rich game terrine and shows us how to make one of France's best-known desserts of creme brulee.

programme.title: The Tower
programme.desc: Crime thriller. Nearly two years since we last saw Sarah Collins, we catch up with her as she is called to the brutal stabbing of a teenager - her investigation soon finds itself at cross purposes with a covert operation led by Kieran Shaw, who is working with Sarah's old partner Steve Bradshaw while he is now deep undercover. Meanwhile, Lizzie Adama is back at Farlow trying to balance her new role as a detective with family life, but her path and Kieran's are about to cross.

programme.title: Unwind with ITV
