programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton presents the series where she meets the owners of beloved pets who have appointments at The Grove Vets. The appointment book is full in this episode as through the doors this time comes 18-year-old cat Paws, whose loss of weight is concerning his owner, Zina the Pomeranian - who is booked in for a spay - and Mara the Boston Terrier, who is undergoing some vital high-tech eye treatment. Elsewhere, whoever has heard of a Labrador being off their food? Dr James Greenwood swaps being a vet to become a detective as he tries to uncover why Rusty is presenting as the saddest dog in the world - who has also, worryingly, lost his appetite - and we meet two owners who go to great lengths to help their dogs' mobility by booking them into a specialist hydrotherapy clinic.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. James then finds himself welcomed into a bouchon, a rustic Lyon institution where he's served a slice of local history in the form of a machon - after experiencing the heartier fare of the region, James ventures to one of the city's many Michelin-starred restaurants to experience some fine dining. James then uses Lyon's inspiration to cook up a tasty pork dish with Lyonnaise potatoes - back in his own kitchen, he then draws on the rustic style of cookery he saw at the bouchon for a rich game terrine and shows us how to make one of France's best-known desserts of creme brulee.

programme.desc: James is joined at his house in the Hampshire countryside by presenter, DJ and I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! star Kelly Brook, chefs Tommy Banks and Alex Dilling, and forager Alysia Vasey.

programme.title: Josie's Taste Of The Westcountry
programme.desc: Proud Bristolian Josie Gibson takes us on a tour of her beloved West Country in a journey of celebration to discover dinner delights, freshly-caught lunches, the best of passionate artisan makers and growers and a few hidden gems to surprise us all - in this episode, Josie heads to Somerset. A county of apples and cheese where ancient caves and landscapes continue to inspire visitors, Josie boards a traditional train to explore the magnificent Somerset coast, gets lessons in oyster-shucking and cider-making, and discovers the secrets of Cheddar Gorge.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh heads to Swindon in this episode to surprise Lorraine, a retired RAF servicewoman and devoted charity volunteer. Lorraine struggles with mobility issues because of a spinal injury and lives with her full-time support team Poppy and Doris, who are both Leonberger dogs - Poppy is a retired therapy dog and Doris is Lorraine's assistance dog who helps with chores such as laundry and fetching household items. The team creates a fabulous low-maintenance garden as a calming retreat for both Lorraine and her canine family, Alan shares the secrets of creating a cut-price chamomile lawn, and Katie creates a Love Your Garden first: a dramatic water feature that doubles as a doggie-paddling pool.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton presents the series where she meets the owners of beloved pets who have appointments at The Grove Vets. The appointment book is full in this episode as through the doors this time comes 18-year-old cat Paws, whose loss of weight is concerning his owner, Zina the Pomeranian - who is booked in for a spay - and Mara the Boston Terrier, who is undergoing some vital high-tech eye treatment. Elsewhere, whoever has heard of a Labrador being off their food? Dr James Greenwood swaps being a vet to become a detective as he tries to uncover why Rusty is presenting as the saddest dog in the world - who has also, worryingly, lost his appetite - and we meet two owners who go to great lengths to help their dogs' mobility by booking them into a specialist hydrotherapy clinic.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. James then finds himself welcomed into a bouchon, a rustic Lyon institution where he's served a slice of local history in the form of a machon - after experiencing the heartier fare of the region, James ventures to one of the city's many Michelin-starred restaurants to experience some fine dining. James then uses Lyon's inspiration to cook up a tasty pork dish with Lyonnaise potatoes - back in his own kitchen, he then draws on the rustic style of cookery he saw at the bouchon for a rich game terrine and shows us how to make one of France's best-known desserts of creme brulee.

Seeking refuge at the village pub, Barnaby learns that Phoebe married Luke after the sudden death of her first husband and Miranda's friend Carter Smith reveals he is helping her with her novel although many in the village doubt that the book really exists - back at the spa, Luke is crushed to death by a training machine soon after being threatened by Carter. After another gruesome discovery, the truth gradually emerges - as the net closes in on the killer, all Barnaby has to worry about is his birthday party, retirement, and welcoming cousin DCI John Barnaby to Causton.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders

Harriet is opposed to the plans of school governor Jamie Cameron and so invites his ex-wife Kate together with her father, racing legend Peter Fossett, to the show - Fossett is annoyed that his fellow judge is club DJ Dave 'Doggy' Day, who knows nothing about cars. Soon afterwards, Doggy is crushed to death under Kate's car and Barnaby thinks the video diaries of two pupils could hold clues to the killing, but a new lead takes him to meet someone at the barn where Duncan Palmer met his death. When the killer turns on him, could Barnaby's first case also be his last?

programme.title: Midsomer Murders

Ben's mother Maggie had also humiliated the investigator - when his body is found in a river, they therefore all come under suspicion. Could a mysterious reference to a moon crater called Bingham hold a clue?

programme.title: Brad Pitt: More Than a Pretty Face
programme.desc: 2022. Director: Adrien Denouette, Thibaut Seve. Dive into the brain of a complex, brilliant and endearing personality, far from the cliche of a world famous movie icon.

programme.title: The Lawless Years
programme.desc: The Nick Joseph Story. 1959. Stars James Gregory, Vic Morrow & Jan Merlin. Ruditsky flips an ex-con to expose a new racketeering play.

programme.title: The Starlost
programme.desc: Deception - Part 1. 1973. Stars Keir Dullea, Gay Rowan & Robin Ward. The trio blunder into a sealed, highly industrialised biosphere. The city is ruled by a paranoid leader preparing for war.

programme.title: Look At Life Shopping for a Queen
programme.desc: 1960. A look into what it takes to replenish an 83,000 ton liner, the Queen Elizabeth, before her next voyage.

programme.title: Green Hornet Strikes Again
programme.desc: Shattering Doom. 1941. Stars Warren Hull. Two reporters are sent to the border where they uncover a group of smugglers. The Green Hornet forces them to reveal the warehouse with explosive results! [S]

programme.title: The Adventures of Sir Lancelot
programme.desc: Witches Brew. 1957. Stars William Russell, Cyril Smith & Ronald Leigh-Hunt. A woman with mystical powers convinces King Bors she is working evil. Merlin is enlisted against these powers. [S]

programme.title: Honey West
programme.desc: 1965. A Neat Little Package. Classic crime series produced by Aaron Spelling and starring Anne Francis. A newsdealer survives a car wreck with amnesia and a mysterious $175,000.

programme.title: Stars In Your Eyes
programme.desc: 1956. Musical. Directed by Maurice Elvey. Stars Nat Jackley, Pat Kirkwood & Bonar Colleano. A group of talented entertainers band together to purchase a run-down theatre to put on a show. [S]

programme.title: The Hostage
programme.desc: 1956. Drama. A South American revolutionary is facing death for murder but the President's daughter in London is taken hostage. Starring Ron Randell. [S]

programme.title: House of Blackmail
programme.desc: 1953. Crime. Directed by Maurice Elvey. An Army officer (William Sylvester) and Carol (Mary Germaine) must solve the murder of a blackmailer or be charged themselves. [S]

programme.title: The Beverly Hillbillies
programme.desc: The Bank Raising. 1964. Stars Buddy Ebsen, Raymond Bailey & Lester Matthews. Invited to the groundbreaking for a new bank, the Clampetts confuse the event with an old-fashioned barn raising. [S]

programme.title: Kentucky Rifle
programme.desc: 1955. Western. Directed by Carl K. Hittleman. Stars Chill Wills & Lance Fuller. While escorting a wagon of rifles, a cowboy must find a way to outsmart the Comanche Indians who plan to steal them. [S]

programme.title: Batman
programme.desc: Ring Around the Riddler. 1967. Stars Adam West, Burt Ward, Yvonne Craig & Joan Collins. The Riddler challenges Batman to a fight in a boxing champion. The Riddler has no plans to play fair. [S]

programme.title: Smokescreen (1964)
programme.desc: 1964. Drama. Directed by Jim O'Connolly. Starring Peter Vaughan, John Carson & Yvonne Romain. A blazing car goes over the cliff to the east of Brighton. Suspicions mount when no body can be found. [S]

programme.title: The Adventures of Robin Hood
programme.desc: The Coming of Robin Hood. 1955. Stars Richard Greene, Victor Woolf & Alan Wheatley. When Robin of Locksley returns home from the Holy Land, he finds Normans are in control everywhere. [S]

programme.title: Give Us A Clue
programme.desc: 1985. The classic game show Give us a Clue hosted by Michael Parkinson, this week's guests are Ronald Allen, Janet Brown, Leslie Crowther, Sue Lloyd, Hank Marvin & Julie Rogers. [S]

programme.title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E
programme.desc: The Secret Sceptre Affair. 1968. Stars Robert Vaughn, David McCallum & Leo G. Carroll. Solo is on a personal mission to help Morgan, who was Solo's commanding officer during the Korean War. [S]

programme.title: The Footage Detectives
programme.desc: Enjoy exclusive and rare footage from the 1968 premiere of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang featuring Dick Van Dyke, as well as a great reel of Melbourne's street cleaners in 1964. [S]

programme.title: Hannay
programme.desc: The Bells of Shoreditch. 1989. Stars: Robert Powell, Paul Rogers & Karen Archer. When his goddaughter is jilted on her wedding day, Hannay finds himself searching for a missing bridegroom. [S]

programme.title: That's My Boy
programme.desc: Go Jump in the Fountain. 1983. Stars Mollie Sugden, Christopher Blake & Jennifer Lonsdale. Angie insists Robert should go out ''with the boys'', not knowing how far out of his rut he will get! [S]

programme.title: The Vise
programme.desc: Side Entrance. 1955. Stars Ron Randell, John Loder & Thea Gregory. Tom wants a divorce. He pretends to go to Paris but he sneaks back to murder his wife and frame it as Barney. [S]

programme.title: Sergeant Cork
programme.desc: The Case of the Vengeful Garnet. 1964. Stars John Barrie, William Gaunt & Charles Morgan. Sergeant Cork is a victim of a minor crime when his wallet was stolen but things take a serious turn. [S]

programme.title: Who Do You Do?
programme.desc: 1972. With Freddie Starr and Peter Goodwright, guest acts such as Janet Brown, Johnny More and Bazz Harris play a number of roles in a series of sketches and songs! [S]

programme.title: The Devil's Hand
programme.desc: 1961. Horror. Directed by William J. Hole Jr. Stars Linda Christian, Robert Alda & Ariadne Welter. A man, haunted by visions of a beautiful woman, winds up in a Satanic cult after meeting her. [S]

programme.title: The Heritage Chart Show with Mike Read
programme.desc: A TOTP style TV Show for Heritage Artists based on the Heritage Chart which is voted on in over 80 countries. Songs you love from popular artists, live and on video with the odd interview.

programme.title: Boris Karloff: The Man Behind
programme.desc: the Monster. 2021. Documentary. Directed by Thomas Hamilton. Features Ron Perlman, Guillermo del Toro. A look at the life and legacy of Boris Karloff, and the history of the genre he personified.

programme.title: The Tower
programme.desc: Crime thriller. Nearly two years since we last saw Sarah Collins, we catch up with her as she is called to the brutal stabbing of a teenager - her investigation soon finds itself at cross purposes with a covert operation led by Kieran Shaw, who is working with Sarah's old partner Steve Bradshaw while he is now deep undercover. Meanwhile, Lizzie Adama is back at Farlow trying to balance her new role as a detective with family life, but her path and Kieran's are about to cross.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton presents the series where she meets the owners of beloved pets who have appointments at The Grove Vets. The appointment book is full in this episode as through the doors this time comes 18-year-old cat Paws, whose loss of weight is concerning his owner, Zina the Pomeranian - who is booked in for a spay - and Mara the Boston Terrier, who is undergoing some vital high-tech eye treatment. Elsewhere, whoever has heard of a Labrador being off their food? Dr James Greenwood swaps being a vet to become a detective as he tries to uncover why Rusty is presenting as the saddest dog in the world - who has also, worryingly, lost his appetite - and we meet two owners who go to great lengths to help their dogs' mobility by booking them into a specialist hydrotherapy clinic.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. James then finds himself welcomed into a bouchon, a rustic Lyon institution where he's served a slice of local history in the form of a machon - after experiencing the heartier fare of the region, James ventures to one of the city's many Michelin-starred restaurants to experience some fine dining. James then uses Lyon's inspiration to cook up a tasty pork dish with Lyonnaise potatoes - back in his own kitchen, he then draws on the rustic style of cookery he saw at the bouchon for a rich game terrine and shows us how to make one of France's best-known desserts of creme brulee.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh heads to Swindon in this episode to surprise Lorraine, a retired RAF servicewoman and devoted charity volunteer. programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton presents the series where she meets the owners of beloved pets who have appointments at The Grove Vets. The appointment book is full in this episode as through the doors this time comes 18-year-old cat Paws, whose loss of weight is concerning his owner, Zina the Pomeranian - who is booked in for a spay - and Mara the Boston Terrier, who is undergoing some vital high-tech eye treatment. Elsewhere, whoever has heard of a Labrador being off their food? Dr James Greenwood swaps being a vet to become a detective as he tries to uncover why Rusty is presenting as the saddest dog in the world - who has also, worryingly, lost his appetite - and we meet two owners who go to great lengths to help their dogs' mobility by booking them into a specialist hydrotherapy clinic.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James ventures to the city of Lyon to explore the two sides of its culinary scene - a visit to the city's famous food market provides plenty of inspiration for his first dish, a Lyonnaise bacon salad. James then finds himself welcomed into a bouchon, a rustic Lyon institution where he's served a slice of local history in the form of a machon - after experiencing the heartier fare of the region, James ventures to one of the city's many Michelin-starred restaurants to experience some fine dining. James then uses Lyon's inspiration to cook up a tasty pork dish with Lyonnaise potatoes - back in his own kitchen, he then draws on the rustic style of cookery he saw at the bouchon for a rich game terrine and shows us how to make one of France's best-known desserts of creme brulee.
